headline: The hyperscaler night split the tape: GOOGL becomes the funding short on a Search miss, MSFT stays the crowded long, crowded SaaS (NOW) unwinds, and a reported MRVL-LITE deal divides the optics trade.
market_read: Desks moved from 'is the AI relief rally real?' (JPM See, 29 Oct: HF de-grossing large enough to favour a semis bounce) to a sharp single-name split. GOOGL fell ~10% on Search ~+12% vs a ~14% bar. UBS (Dwyer, 28 Oct) calls the feedback the worst since early 2025, and Bernstein and Jefferies (29/28 Oct) put it back in the short/funding-short bucket. MSFT (Azure +48% cc, 49-50% guide) stays the crowded megacap long that Barclays still sees adding buyers; the after-hours fade came on its funding comment (UBS, Jefferies). For the AI supply chain the read is 'no incremental capex help' (Jefferies Beavington, 29 Oct) against BofA research (Arya) lifting CY26/27 AI capex growth, while JPM's desk (Tyler, 29 Oct) sees the AI theme being sold for a defensive / ex-AI rotation. ORCL's investor day is the credit-positive surprise (GS, MS).

up.why: Barclays (Rand, 28 Oct) says positioning already leaned long but still had incremental buyers and expects MSFT to be a preferred TMT long. Jefferies (Wong, 28 Oct) and UBS (Dwyer, 29 Oct) both call it the most crowded Mag7 long. MSFT is not in the Bloomberg X rising/falling list (data through 28 Oct, pre-print) and has no HOT/BULL analog in monitor.json, so the crowding call rests on desk evidence alone. Over 1-5 days the beat supports it as the place to hide inside megacaps. Over 2-4 weeks, crowding plus funding-language risk makes it vulnerable to any capex or OpenAI-concentration wobble (Jefferies notes investors asking how much of Azure is OAI-driven).
up.confirm: Desks report new long-only buying, not just HF adds; Azure guide holds through AMZN's print; no debt/equity-raise headline.
up.weaken: A debt or equity raise announcement, or desks start calling it a source of funds as megacap rotation broadens.

up.why: Bernstein's crowding work had ORCL near the least-crowded end on 28 Oct (prior ledger). The investor day (FCF positive in 2H FY28, ~$30bn FY29 FCF, raises capped at $20bn) drew positive feedback and an 11% intraday move (MS Wigg, 28 Oct); GS (Arruda, 29 Oct) calls it the key event for levered AI credit, and Bernstein (Seidman, 29 Oct) sees the bear case quieting. ORCL is not in the Bloomberg X mover lists and has no analog in monitor.json. Over 1-5 days, follow-through depends on credit spreads (GS: 'still need to see spreads respond'). Over 2-4 weeks, an under-owned name with a funding endpoint can keep re-rating.
up.confirm: ORCL CDS and bonds tighten in the credit workbook; desks report shorts covering or long-only re-entry.
up.weaken: Spreads don't move, or new financing or BYOH counterparty headlines revive the funding debate.

up.why: GOOGL's Search/YouTube miss makes META's ad beat look better: META rose after hours (UBS Dwyer, 28 Oct), and Jefferies (Wong, 28 Oct) asks whether it is now an even more attractive long. META is not in the Bloomberg X mover lists and has no analog in monitor.json. Over 1-5 days, expect relative-pair flows (long META / short GOOGL). Over 2-4 weeks, it hinges on the Muse/agent narrative that the desks blame for GOOGL's Search worries.
up.confirm: Desks report pair trades or long-only adds; Muse engagement data keep improving.
up.weaken: Pressure from the $98bn AI-funding share sale returns, or AMZN ad strength dilutes the share-gain story.

up.why: If MRVL buys LITE, COHR becomes the last large independent laser/optics supplier, and JPM (Meyers, 29 Oct) says it 'should be in the spotlight'. This is a single-desk idea, not positioning data. Bernstein (Seidman, 29 Oct) hears the deal as unlikely, and COHR is not in the Bloomberg X movers or analogs. Over 1-5 days it trades on deal headlines. Over 2-4 weeks it needs confirmation of the deal or customer dual-sourcing commentary.
up.confirm: MRVL/LITE confirm terms; hyperscalers or desks cite single-source risk; COHR attention rises on Bloomberg X.
up.weaken: The deal is denied or collapses, or LITE trades as stand-alone again.

up.why: Jefferies (Beavington, 29 Oct) says the first GaN power-electronics orders are 'hugely incremental': AIXA is no longer only opto, and steady order momentum implies well above the 800m consensus. This is a single desk voice, and AIXA has no Bloomberg X or analog data in monitor.json. Over 1-5 days it is a results-driven move. Over 2-4 weeks it depends on GaN order cadence (ties to the 800V DC-power theme).
up.confirm: Further GaN/power orders; other desks or research pick up the GaN-for-800V angle.
up.weaken: Orders revert to opto-only, or the 4Q order guide disappoints.

down.why: Several desks agree. UBS (Dwyer, 28 Oct) says feedback is the worst since early 2025. Bernstein (Seidman, 29 Oct) calls it a funding short into year-end. Jefferies (Wong, 28 Oct) says it was less shorted than in mid-September, so there is room for shorts to build. MS (Wigg, 28 Oct) says the secular AI bear case is back. monitor.json (through 28 Oct, pre-print) had GOOG at HOT 53.1 / BULL 43.5, both in the 40-<60 band; own-history 5-session analogs show a median of +1.4% (70% up, n=40) for HOT and -0.2% (46% up, n=46) for BULL. Those were pre-gap, so they are no guide to the post-miss path. Over 1-5 days, dip buyers have little to lean on: no capex raise, a 4Q comp/FX headwind guide and Cloud-margin headwinds from third-party capacity. Over 2-4 weeks, watch whether the TPU (OAI/OCI) story re-emerges as the long case.
down.confirm: Estimate cuts land (UBS: 'bias to estimates feels lower'), desks report short-interest rising, and the Search-share narrative spreads to AMZN/META prints.
down.weaken: TPU external-sales disclosure or Gemini 4 Carbon traction pulls in long-only value buyers, or the gap fills quickly on short covering.

down.why: NOW was the favourite large-cap app long into the print (Barclays, 28 Oct, prior ledger). After the cRPO miss and an 18.5% cc 4Q guide, Barclays (Rand, 28 Oct) and UBS (Ruple, 28 Oct) both say the crowding explains the ~13-20% drop, and SaaS peers fell with it (MS: CRM/WDAY -5%, HUBS/TEAM -6%). This is crowding unwinding, not a new bear thesis: Bernstein (29 Oct) rates it '+ -'. NOW has no Bloomberg X or analog data in monitor.json. Over 1-5 days, expect continued liquidation. Over 2-4 weeks, a cleaner base could form once holders exit, because the AI ACV target was raised to $1.7bn.
down.confirm: Desks report long-only exits and the SaaS crowding basket keeps lagging.
down.weaken: The cRPO accounting noise (the VA renewal flagged by Bernstein pre-print) is explained away on callbacks and buyers step in.

down.why: The reported MRVL-LITE deal hit MRVL about 11% pre-market (GS, 29 Oct). JPM (Meyers, 29 Oct) hears holders call it expensive, with dilution and China/antitrust risk. BofA research (Arya) relayed the same overhangs (customer conflict, size). The prior ledger had MRVL still 'rather crowded' (UBS, 27 Oct), so an expensive deal hits a long base. Desks diverge on whether the deal happens: JPM calls the news credible, Bernstein hears it as unlikely. MRVL has no Bloomberg X or analog data. Over 1-5 days it is headline-driven. Over 2-4 weeks it depends on terms and financing mix.
down.confirm: The deal is confirmed with heavy stock consideration; desks report long-only exits.
down.weaken: The deal is denied, or terms show accretion and laser-supply security is reframed as an AVGO-style moat.

down.why: Samsung turned negative on an OP miss and no added 2026 shareholder return that some investors had hoped for, after Hynix raised the bar (Jefferies O'Mara, 29 Oct; GS: Samsung -4%). Fundamentals stayed firm on the call: HBM share in line with DRAM share, best HBM4 base-die yield, and demand above supply into 2027 (management, via Jefferies). This is a capital-return disappointment, not a demand break. Samsung has no Bloomberg X or analog data in monitor.json. Over 1-5 days it lags Hynix. Over 2-4 weeks the late-January return announcement is the catalyst.
down.confirm: Foreign selling continues; Korea desks report rotation into Hynix.
down.weaken: Return framework headlines come earlier than January, or HBM4 share gains are confirmed by NVDA supply-chain checks.

themes.title: Hyperscaler capex: 'no incremental help' vs 'capex raised'
themes.text: Jefferies (Beavington, 29 Oct) says MSFT's CY26 capex trim to $170bn (third-party delays) and GOOGL's unchanged $195-205bn add nothing to near-term semis capex expectations, because the rate of increase matters. BofA research (Arya, relayed by Franco, 29 Oct) instead lifts CY26/27 AI capex growth to 99%/54% (from 98%/37%) and cites record GPU-hour prices implying under one-year paybacks. The desks frame it as a timing issue (third-party capacity shifting into 2H), not reduced appetite (GS Arruda, Bernstein Seidman).

themes.title: Optics consolidation: is MRVL-LITE real, and who benefits?
themes.text: JPM (Meyers) calls the Bloomberg report credible and frames it as MRVL buying scarce laser capacity, sold out into 2029. Bernstein (Seidman) hears it as widely viewed as unlikely. Both sides of the deal are unhappy: MRVL holders say expensive, LITE holders say it caps upside. COHR is flagged as the last independent laser player. Gaetano Research (independent Substack, 29 Oct, 'Marvell's Optical Ambition') arrived but was not read in this run.

themes.title: AI-theme rotation vs semis-bounce case
themes.text: JPM's market-intelligence desk (Tyler, 29 Oct) sees the AI theme being sold with a defensive bias, while discretionary and financials bid as the ex-AI 'broadening' trade, and Jefferies quant (Peramunetilleke, via Beavington) markets 'Diversifying away from A.I.' (AI earnings growth slowing to ~30% in 2027). JPM APAC (See, 29 Oct) argues HF de-grossing was large enough that semis can keep bouncing on 2027 capex upside and ROI clarity. The disagreement is open, and GS (Arruda) expects dips to get bought while credit stabilises.

themes.title: ORCL as the credit linchpin
themes.text: GS (Arruda) calls ORCL's funding cap and FCF path more consequential for the levered AI-infrastructure complex than either hyperscaler print, but says spreads still need to confirm. MS (Wigg) notes semis rose on ORCL's lower FY29 capex because BYOH shifts capex to others rather than removing it.

coverage_gaps: No DAMNANG or SemiAnalysis e-mail arrived in the window, so there was no independent-author check on the memory or optics reads.
The Gaetano Research Substack on MRVL's optical ambition (29 Oct 05:24Z) and TMT Breakout's GOOGL/MSFT first takes were screened but not read.
Bloomberg X attention and the HOT/BULL analogs in monitor.json run through 28 Oct, before the GOOGL/MSFT/NOW prints. The step-3 rebuild refreshes them, so the 'why' fields cite pre-print levels.
MSFT, ORCL, META, NOW, MRVL, COHR, SAMSUNG and AIXA have no HOT/BULL analog rows in monitor.json, so for them the read rests on desk evidence only.
AMZN, INTC and SNDK report after today's close; only the JPM buyside sentiment scores (+4 INTC, +2 SNDK) were logged.
source_notes: Channel outlook-com via desk_mail_collect.ps1; inbox lag 0 h; 1,148 messages screened, 389 bodies pulled, ~44 read in full or in part (registered desk senders first). Messages before about 13:02Z on 28 Oct were covered by the 28 Oct review and were not re-logged.
Desk and specialist-sales voices carry no ratings or PTs. Ratings and PTs quoted in BofA one-liners belong to BofA Research and are logged as 'Research relay', not desk opinion.
Desk tickers differ slightly on GOOGL's Search growth (+11.8% UBS vs +12% MS/Jefferies) and YouTube growth (+9% to +11%). Each figure is attributed as given, not reconciled.
Weighting is editorial: multi-desk agreement (GOOGL, NOW) weighs more than single-desk ideas (COHR, AIXA), and pre-market moves are logged as tape, not conviction.
